To move beyond this oracle setting, we further develop an external RiskOcc predictor, a perception module that estimates risk-aware occupancy directly from sensor inputs. The competitive performance validates the representation's feasibility.

AI.tldr: Risk-aware occupancy (RiskOcc) and RRDrive improve multimodal trajectory prediction by providing a dense, temporally aligned, and queryable scene representation, enhancing candidate generation and ranking; validated on RiskOcc4D-NAVSIM with an external RiskOcc predictor showing competitive performance and potential beyond oracle baselines.
AI.motivation: Sparse scene representations lead to low-quality candidate generation and unreliable ranking among geometrically similar trajectories in multimodal trajectory prediction for end-to-end autonomous driving.
AI.method: Introduce RRDrive with risk-aware occupancy (RiskOcc) as a dense, temporally aligned, trajectory-queryable representation. Use its global structure to guide multimodal generation and candidate-conditioned risk queries to refine selection. Build RiskOcc4D-NAVSIM with automatic risk annotations. Develop an external RiskOcc predictor that estimates risk-aware occupancy from sensor inputs to move beyond oracle settings.
AI.result: On a register-based baseline, 19.74% of candidates are bad/poor; oracle-best ranks 33.9th on average. RRDrive achieves selected-trajectory PDMS = 0.951 (1.5% relative gain over baseline 0.937); average candidate PDMS improves by 7.7%. In challenging scenes, candidate PDMS improves by 30.2% and Spearman correlation among good candidates rises from 0.26 to 0.67 (+0.41). An external RiskOcc predictor demonstrates feasibility by competitive performance without oracle.
AI.conclusion: Risk-aware occupancy is a feasible and effective representation for guiding high-quality multimodal trajectory generation and fine-grained candidate selection; it enhances both generation quality and ranking, and the external predictor showcases practical applicability beyond oracle-based evaluation.

title: Quantization-Aware Kalman Estimation for Diffusion Sampling
summary: Quantization offers a practical path to deploying diffusion models with reduced memory and computation, but aggressive compression can cause quantized outputs to deviate substantially from their full-precision counterparts. Sampling-stage correction methods seek to compensate for such deviations during sampling, but existing approaches rely primarily on local information and underexploit trajectory history, limiting their ability to correct errors that propagate across timesteps. In this work, we formulate sampling with a quantized denoiser as an online estimation problem, using the history of quantized denoiser outputs to recover the underlying full-precision outputs required by the sampler. We propose QuAKE, a Quantization-Aware Kalman Estimator that combines a smooth trajectory prior with a conditional Gaussian observation model. At each sampling step, QuAKE recursively updates the posterior over the output window in closed form and feeds its posterior mean to the sampler. QuAKE is a lightweight plug-and-play corrector that requires no modification to the quantized network and naturally supports arbitrary high-order multistep ODE samplers. Experiments across W4A4-quantized text-to-image diffusion models show that QuAKE consistently outperforms existing methods in reducing the distributional discrepancy from full-precision sampling.

AI.tldr: Introduces QuAKE, a Kalman-estimator–based sampling-time correction for quantized diffusion models; leverages history of quantized denoiser outputs to estimate full-precision outputs, improving fidelity to full-precision sampling; plug-and-play with high-order multistep ODE samplers; demonstrates improved distributional fidelity on W4A4 quantized T2I models.
AI.motivation: Quantization reduces memory and compute for diffusion models but can cause large deviations from full-precision outputs. Existing sampling corrections rely on local information and neglect trajectory history, limiting their ability to fix errors that propagate across timesteps. A method that uses online estimation over the denoiser output trajectory can better recover full-precision outputs.
AI.method: Propose QuAKE, a Quantization-Aware Kalman Estimator. It treats sampling with a quantized denoiser as an online estimation problem, using the history of quantized denoiser outputs to infer the underlying full-precision outputs required by the sampler. QuAKE uses a smooth trajectory prior and a conditional Gaussian observation model, performing recursive, closed-form posterior updates over the output window at each step and feeding the posterior mean to the sampler. It is plug-and-play, requiring no modification to the quantized network and supports arbitrary high-order multistep ODE samplers.
AI.result: Across W4A4-quantized text-to-image diffusion models, QuAKE consistently outperforms existing sampling-time correction methods by reducing the distributional discrepancy compared to full-precision sampling.
AI.conclusion: QuAKE provides a lightweight, trajectory-history–aware corrector that integrates with quantized diffusion models without altering the quantized network, improving fidelity to full-precision sampling and being compatible with high-order multistep samplers.

title: M2G-LLM: Enhancing Clinical Prediction via Multimodal Graph Reasoning and LLM Context Injection
summary: Integrating diverse data modalities --- such as clinical notes, laboratory results, and medical imaging --- is essential for advancing clinical decision-making. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown remarkable performance in processing unstructured clinical text, their limited capacity to incorporate non-text modalities hinders their broader utility in healthcare applications. Here, we introduce M2G-LLM (Multimodal MedGraph-LLM), a novel framework that enhances LLMs with multimodal integration and alignment via Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). Our approach models temporal relationships between patient visits, propagates information across clinically similar patients, and aligns heterogeneous data sources to construct enriched multimodal context vectors. These vectors are injected into the intermediate layers of the LLM, enabling joint reasoning over textual and non-textual modalities. We evaluate M2G-LLM on the MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-CXR datasets, demonstrating improvements in clinical prediction tasks over strong baseline models. Our results highlight the promise of combining the language understanding of LLMs with the relational reasoning capabilities of GNNs for comprehensive, multimodal healthcare analysis.

AI.tldr: M2G-LLM fuses LLMs with graph neural networks to integrate multimodal clinical data (text, labs, images) and model temporal and relational structure for improved predictions on MIMIC datasets.
AI.motivation: LLMs excel at unstructured text but struggle to incorporate non-text modalities and relational temporal information in Electronic Health Records (EHRs); a unified framework is needed to align heterogeneous sources and exploit patient similarity and visit sequences.
AI.method: Construct M2G-LLM: build multimodal context vectors by modeling temporal relationships between patient visits, propagating information across clinically similar patients, and aligning heterogeneous data sources via a GNN. Inject the enriched context vectors into intermediate LLM layers to enable joint textual and non-textual reasoning.
AI.result: On MIMIC-IV and MIMIC-CXR, M2G-LLM achieves superior clinical prediction performance compared to strong baselines, demonstrating the benefit of combining LLM language understanding with GNN-based relational multimodal reasoning.
AI.conclusion: Combining LLMs with GNN-based multimodal alignment and temporal propagation holds promise for comprehensive, multimodal healthcare analysis and decision support.

title: MA-LIPP: Cooperative Multi-Agent Load-Aware Informative Path Planning for Heterogeneous Robot Teams
summary: Field robotics missions often require physical samples to be returned to laboratories for analysis, making path planning inherently load-aware and order-dependent as accumulated samples increase payload and traversal energy costs. In single-robot Load-Aware Informative Path Planning (LIPP), this rigidly couples sensing with hauling: a solitary robot must transport every collected sample, forcing frequent depot returns that severely restrict its spatial coverage. Heterogeneous multi-robot teams can overcome this bottleneck by dividing labor---enabling high-precision samplers to collect while high-capacity carriers handle transport. However, this introduces a complex coordination challenge regarding when, where, what, and to whom handoffs should occur on top of the LIPP problem. To address this tightly coupled problem, we introduce Multi-Agent LIPP (MA-LIPP), which enables teams to cooperate through asynchronous "dead drops," allowing one robot to deposit samples for another to retrieve later without requiring synchronous rendezvous. We formulate MA-LIPP as an exact Mixed-Integer Quadratic Program (MIQP) alongside a scalable Pairwise Large-Neighborhood Search (LNS) heuristic for complex real-world applications. The heuristic matches exact optima in $95.5\%$ of certified cases and reduces weighted posterior variance by $16.1$--$19.8\%$ relative to a sequential baseline on larger instances of up to 12 robots, providing a robust framework for cooperative physical-sampling missions.

AI.tldr: MA-LIPP enables cooperative, load-aware informative path planning for multi-robot sampling via asynchronous dead drops, combining an exact MIQP formulation with a scalable Large-Neighborhood Search heuristic; it shows near-optimal performance and substantial uncertainty reduction on up to 12 robots.
AI.motivation: Single-robot load-aware planning tightly couples sensing and hauling, limiting coverage. Multi-robot teams can split sensing and transport, but coordination for handoffs adds complexity. MA-LIPP addresses this with asynchronous dead drops to avoid rendezvous constraints.
AI.method: Formulate MA-LIPP as an exact Mixed-Integer Quadratic Program (MIQP) for optimal coordination and path planning with load constraints and handoffs; develop a scalable Pairwise Large-Neighborhood Search (LNS) heuristic to solve larger instances efficiently; introduce asynchronous dead drops to enable non-simultaneous handoffs between robots.
AI.result: The LNS heuristic matches exact optimal solutions in 95.5% of certified cases and reduces weighted posterior variance by 16.1% to 19.8% relative to a sequential baseline on instances with up to 12 robots.
AI.conclusion: Ma-LIPP provides a robust, scalable framework for cooperative physical-sampling missions, enabling effective collaboration between sensing and transport roles and improving coverage and informational value in multi-robot missions; demonstrated performance gains on moderately sized teams.

title: LogicTrack: Auditing Reasoning Trajectories of Large Language Models with Formal Logic Solvers
summary: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning has been shown to improve the performance of large language models (LLMs), yet existing optimization methods largely rely on outcome-based feedback, leaving the logical validity of intermediate reasoning steps largely unverified. To address the gap whereby LLMs arrive at correct final answers through logically flawed intermediate reasoning chains, we propose LogicTrack, a neuro-symbolic framework that audits reasoning trajectories by auto-formalizing each reasoning step into symbolic representations and verifying it with automated theorem provers. LogicTrack introduces Solver-Based Backtracking Reward (SBR), a step-wise scoring mechanism that quantifies logical soundness and guides backtracking tree search at inference time. We further extend LogicTrack to construct supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data with backtracking traces from its trajectories, enabling fine-tuned models to internalize step-wise auditing as an intrinsic capability. Extensive experiments across 8 reasoning benchmarks and 7 LLMs demonstrate that LogicTrack effectively improves both the verifiability of reasoning chains and final answer pass rate, thereby enhancing overall CoT quality and trustworthiness in high-stakes domains.

AI.tldr: LogicTrack: a neuro-symbolic CoT auditing framework with solver-based backtracking rewards and backtracking-based SFT data that improves reasoning verifiability and final answer accuracy across multiple benchmarks and LLMs.
AI.motivation: Current CoT methods rely on outcome-based feedback and do not verify intermediate reasoning steps, enabling logically flawed chains to produce correct final answers; there is a need for auditing reasoning trajectories to increase verifiability and trust in high-stakes domains.
AI.method: Auto-formalize each reasoning step into symbolic representations and verify with automated theorem provers; introduce Solver-Based Backtracking Reward (SBR) to score logical soundness and guide backtracking search during inference; extend to construct supervised fine-tuning data with backtracking traces for intrinsic auditing capability in models.
AI.result: Across 8 reasoning benchmarks and 7 LLMs, LogicTrack improves verifiability of reasoning chains and final answer pass rate, enhancing overall CoT quality and trustworthiness in high-stakes domains.
AI.conclusion: LogicTrack provides a verifiable, trustworthy CoT framework by integrating neuro-symbolic reasoning, formal verification, and backtracking-guided training; its approach shows robust gains across multiple benchmarks and models.

title: When Online Adaptation Hurts: Parameter-Frozen Test-Time Ensembling for Continual Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Medical image segmenters often get worse when sites, scanner vendors, or protocols change. Continual test-time adaptation (CTTA) addresses this problem without target labels, but it can be impossible to update a model on a non-stationary stream and can lead to a lot of errors. We examine a more reasonable and meaningful alternative: parameter-frozen inference enhancement(PIE). We use a source-trained segmenter that learns about anatomy-preserving scale and flip views, maps their predictions back to the native location, and averages the probabilities. We do not modify the weights of the model or the normalization statistics. On a cardiac MRI stream from M\&Ms, which is trained on vendor A and evaluated sequentially on vendors B, C, and D, PIE has 0.7786 mean Dice, compared to 0.7680 for source-only inference and 0.7388--0.7416 for five other online-adaptation baselines. The controlled ablations show that performance saturates at 28 views, and confidence weighting, class-prior correction, connected-component filtering, morphological refinement, and inter-slice smoothing have no effect or cause negative transfer. Qualitative results on cardiac MRI and fundus images are also consistent with the frozen ensemble keeping thinner and nested anatomical structures. These results provide a strong, stable baseline for medical CTTA and expose an important failure mode: adaptation and handcrafted refinement can be less reliable than carefully designed inference.

AI.tldr: A parameter-frozen inference technique (PIE) using anatomy-preserving transformations and ensemble averaging improves CTTA performance without updating model weights, outperforming source-only and several online-adaptation baselines on a multi-vendor cardiac MRI stream.
AI.motivation: CTTA methods can be unstable and error-prone on non-stationary streams; a reliable, training-free inference approach is needed that preserves anatomy and minimizes negative transfer.
AI.method: Apply a source-trained segmenter to multiple anatomy-preserving views (scale and flips), map predictions back to native coordinates, and average probabilities. Do not modify weights or normalization statistics. Treat transformed predictions as a frozen ensemble. Evaluate on a cardiac MRI stream (vendor A to B/C/D). Conduct ablations showing 28 views suffices; confidence weighting, class-prior correction, connected-component filtering, morphological refinement, and inter-slice smoothing have little or negative effect.
AI.result: PIE achieves mean Dice 0.7786, higher than source-only 0.7680 and five online-adaptation baselines at 0.7388–0.7416. Ablations indicate performance saturates around 28 views, and additional refinements do not improve and may harm. Qualitative results show the frozen ensemble preserves thinner and nested anatomical structures, indicating a robust, inference-only advantage.
AI.conclusion: Inference-time design with frozen weights can surpass adaptation-based methods; reliance on adaptation and handcrafted refinements can be less reliable than well-designed inference. PIE provides a strong, stable baseline for medical CTTA and highlights a key failure mode of heavy adaptation.

title: TierKV: Long-Context On-Device LLMs via Predictive Multi-Tier KV Caching
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are moving onto mobile devices for increasingly diverse workloads over text, images, video, and audio. These applications often require long contexts, making the Key-Value (KV) cache a dominant memory bottleneck because it grows linearly with sequence length and is accessed at every decoding step. Prior work reduces KV-cache footprint through low-rank compression, token eviction, or flash offloading, but the resulting reconstruction overhead, irreversible token loss, or I/O stalls can offset the benefit of saving memory. We present TierKV, a mobile LLM inference framework built on Predictive Multi-Tier Cache Optimization (PMCO). Before decoding starts, PMCO predicts future cache demand from prefill hidden states and jointly assigns tokens to exact, low-rank, and flash-offloaded tiers under the device memory and accuracy budgets. This formulation retains access to the full context, removes the circular dependency of reactive eviction, and admits a closed-form solver that selects tier boundaries and per-layer ranks at runtime. Across eight text, vision, and audio models on three mobile SoCs, TierKV improves prefill throughput by up to 17.6x over existing mobile LLM frameworks, reduces RAM-resident KV cache by 12.5-34%, thereby enabling substantially longer contexts under the same memory budget, while incurring only minor accuracy degradation.

AI.tldr: TierKV uses Predictive Multi-Tier Cache Optimization to partition the KV cache for mobile LLMs across exact, low-rank, and flash-offloaded tiers, yielding large throughput gains and RAM savings with minimal accuracy loss.
AI.motivation: KV-cache growth with sequence length is the primary memory bottleneck in mobile LLM inference; existing reductions (low-rank compression, eviction, flash offload) trade memory for reconstruction cost, data loss, or I/O stalls, preventing long-context usage.
AI.method: Before decoding, PMCO predicts future cache demand from prefill hidden states and jointly assigns tokens to exact, low-rank, and flash-offloaded tiers under device memory and accuracy budgets. It uses a closed-form solver to determine tier boundaries and per-layer ranks at runtime, avoiding reactive eviction.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on eight models (text, vision, audio) across three mobile SoCs shows up to 17.6× prefill throughput gains, 12.5–34% reduction in RAM-resident KV cache, enabling longer contexts with minor accuracy degradation.
AI.conclusion: TierKV demonstrates that predictive, analytically solvable tiered caching can substantially improve mobile LLM inference by balancing latency, memory, and accuracy, and generalizes across modalities and hardware.

title: OpenRoIS: A Community-Driven Open-Source Middleware Implementing the Robotic Interaction Service (RoIS) Framework for Physical Robots and Virtual Agents
comment: Submitted for presentation at the 2027 IEEE/SICE International Symposium on System Integration (SII), Kobe, Japan
summary: Service applications for human-robot interaction are commonly written against the hardware-specific interfaces of one platform, so a change of hardware forces a rewrite of the application. The Robotic Interaction Service (RoIS) Framework 2.0, standardized by the Object Management Group (OMG), addresses this fragmentation by defining a platform-independent model in which Service Applications interact with Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) Engines through standardized interfaces and hardware-independent symbolic messages. A specification alone, however, does not provide the maintained implementation, Software Development Kits (SDKs), and adapters needed for practical adoption. This paper presents OpenRoIS, a community-driven open-source middleware providing a concrete implementation of the RoIS Framework 2.0. It takes the position that an openly developed, paradigm-neutral implementation is what carries the standard from specification to practice. OpenRoIS contributes a recursive engine architecture in which a single engine class realizes the main and sub HRI Engine roles, an internal five-method component contract distinct from the five external RoIS interfaces, a mapping of those interfaces onto JSON-RPC 2.0 over WebSocket, a single-source-of-truth type pipeline that generates three consistent language stacks, TypeScript and C# client SDKs that include web and Unity support, and a Python adapter SDK that includes ROS 2 support. Through the common RoIS interfaces, a Service Application can address physical robots and virtual agents over the internet. All source code, interface types, and documentation are released under the Apache-2.0 license and openly developed at https://openrois.org/.

AI.tldr: OpenRoIS provides a concrete, open-source implementation of the RoIS 2.0 framework, enabling platform-independent human-robot interaction through a unified engine, JSON-RPC over WebSocket, and multi-language SDKs.
AI.motivation: Fragmentation arises from hardware-specific interfaces and the lack of practical, maintained implementations for RoIS 2.0; a community-driven, open-source implementation is needed to move the standard from specification to practice and ensure sustainable adoption.
AI.method: OpenRoIS introduces a recursive engine architecture (single engine class for main and sub HRI Engine roles), an internal five-method contract distinct from the five external RoIS interfaces, maps RoIS interfaces to JSON-RPC 2.0 over WebSocket, employs a single-source-of-truth pipeline generating three language stacks, and provides TypeScript and C# client SDKs (web and Unity), plus a Python adapter SDK with ROS 2 support. All components are released under Apache-2.0; development is at openrois.org.
AI.result: A practical, open-source middleware that enables Service Applications to address physical robots and virtual agents over the internet, with cross-language SDKs, adapters, and ROS 2 support, aligning practical deployments with the RoIS 2.0 standard.
AI.conclusion: OpenRoIS demonstrates how a paradigm-neutral, community-driven implementation can accelerate standard adoption by bridging specification and practice and enabling interoperable, platform-agnostic HRI development.

title: PolyBridgeBench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Physics-Grounded Bridge Design
summary: Multimodal large language models, or MLLMs, perform well at visual understanding and structured generation, yet these capabilities do not establish whether an engineering design will work when executed. Existing benchmarks assess spatial reasoning, structural validity, or physics-grounded construction, but they do not determine whether MLLMs can synthesize complete load-bearing structures and repair them after simulator execution exposes a failure. We introduce PolyBridgeBench, an executable benchmark for multimodal bridge design. A model receives a visual scene and structured engineering constraints and generates a complete node--member--material topology. Deterministic legality checks gate execution in a native dynamic physics simulation. Following an execution failure, the benchmark returns temporal visual evidence from the failed rollout and evaluates repair under a fixed interaction budget. Separate measurements of deterministic validity, dynamic functional success, and post-failure recovery identify the stage at which design fails. Experiments with six representative MLLMs across 189 levels expose a substantial gap between deterministic validity and dynamic success, pronounced sensitivity to material budgets, and limited post-failure recovery under the primary strict-budget setting.

AI.tldr: Introduces PolyBridgeBench, an executable benchmark for multimodal bridge design that evaluates LLM-based designers on creating complete node–member–material topologies, validating them deterministically, simulating their dynamics, and repairing failures within a fixed budget. It reveals a gap between static (deterministic) validity and dynamic execution success, sensitivity to material budgets, and limited post-failure recovery.
AI.motivation: Current MLLMs excel at perception and planning in abstract tasks but lack benchmarks that require integrating design generation with physics-simulated execution and repair, especially for load-bearing structures.
AI.method: Provide the model with a visual scene and engineering constraints; require generation of a complete topology (nodes, members, materials); gate execution with deterministic legality checks; run a native physics simulator to test performance; on failure, provide temporal visual evidence and evaluate repair under a fixed interaction budget; compute separate metrics for deterministic validity, dynamic functional success, and post-failure recovery across multiple levels and models.
AI.result: Experiments with six representative MLLMs across 189 levels show a substantial gap between deterministic validity and dynamic success, strong sensitivity to material budgets, and limited post-failure recovery under the primary strict-budget setting.
AI.conclusion: Benchmarks that couple design synthesis with physics execution and repair are needed; current MLLMs struggle to produce executable, repairable load-bearing designs within budget constraints, indicating key failure modes and areas for model and benchmark improvements.

title: P$^3$-SAM: SAM with Perceptual Parallel Prompt for Few-Shot Strip Steel Surface Defect Segmentation
comment: Accepted by ICME 2026, 6 pages, 3 figures. Corresponding authors: Anpeng Wang and Runmin Cong
summary: Few-shot semantic segmentation (FSS) of strip steel surface defects (S$^3$D) has posed significant challenges distinct from natural scenes. Unlike natural images, S$^3$D task exhibits unique characteristics including low local contrast, uneven illumination, and complex fine-grained texture patterns. Although recent methods based on Segment Anything Model (SAM) have shown promise in FSS on natural images by leveraging SAM's powerful pre-trained representations, these unique industrial characteristics of S$^3$D images lead to performance drop when directly applying SAM to industrial defect scenarios. In this paper, we propose a novel Perceptual Parallel Prompt (P$^3$) framework that empowers SAM, creating the P$^3$-SAM model to address these challenges through two core strategies. First, we develop a Perceptual-Optimized Encoding (POE) strategy that enhances local contrast and preserves critical texture details for S$^3$D segmentation. Second, we introduce the Parallel Prompt Generator (PPG) strategy that simultaneously generates both semantic and spatial prompts, enabling comprehensive guidance for SAM's decoder across varying images. Extensive experiments on three few-shot S$^3$D benchmarks demonstrate that P$^3$-SAM achieves state-of-the-art performance, with particularly notable improvements of 12.00% in mIoU on Surface Defects-4i dataset.

AI.tldr: P^3-SAM adapts SAM for few-shot strip steel defect segmentation via Perceptual-Optimized Encoding and a Parallel Prompt Generator, yielding state-of-the-art results and a notable 12.0 percentage-point mIoU gain on Surface Defects-4i.
AI.motivation: Industrial S^3D images exhibit low local contrast, uneven illumination, and fine-grained textures that degrade SAM's zero-shot performance on natural images when applied to defects.
AI.method: Perceptual-Optimized Encoding (POE) improves local contrast and texture preservation; Parallel Prompt Generator (PPG) jointly creates semantic and spatial prompts to guide SAM's decoder across diverse defect images.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on three few-shot S^3D benchmarks show state-of-the-art performance, with a particularly notable 12.00% mIoU improvement on the Surface Defects-4i dataset.
AI.conclusion: P^3-SAM effectively customizes SAM for industrial defect segmentation, addressing domain-specific perceptual challenges and delivering substantial performance gains, suggesting potential applicability to other domain-adapted FSS tasks.

title: SWE-Proof: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World Issues with Machine-Checked Proofs?
summary: Ensuring the correctness of LLM-generated code is a core challenge for modern software engineering. Benchmarks for agentic code generation check correctness with held-out test suites, which are inherently incomplete and increasingly susceptible to memorization. Formal verification avoids both problems, but existing work covers only standalone tasks whose specifications are given as input, not real issues, which touch large repositories and state intent in vague natural language. We present Benchproofer, a pipeline that turns a coding task with a known correct patch into a formally verified one: it writes a specification for the new code, summarizes the existing functions that code calls with axioms, and admits an instance only after mechanical and adversarial gates agree. Applying it to SWE-bench Verified yields SWE-Proof, 500 real issues whose correctness is formally verified rather than tested, and it extends to SWE-bench Pro. Across two frontier models, verification catches what tests miss: a quarter to a half of test-passing patches admit counterexamples, which a structured natural-language specification does not fix, while a correct formal one lifts resolution from 85% to 95% for Opus 4.8. Writing that specification is the hard part: models that must write their own gain nothing over an unaided baseline, and only 62% of their specifications pass our audit. The usual failure is faithfulness, a specification that constrains part of the required behavior and leaves the rest free. Specification quality still tracks the outcome, failing on 89% of unresolved instances against 47% of resolved ones, making faithful specification synthesis a concrete open problem.

AI.tldr: Benchproofer converts coding tasks with known patches into formally verified patches, yielding SWE-Proof (500 issues) and extending to SWE-bench Pro, and shows formal verification catches errors tests miss but highlighting that generating faithful specifications is the main bottleneck.
AI.motivation: Test-based benchmarks for LLM-generated code are incomplete and prone to memorization; formal verification could be more robust but existing work covers only isolated tasks with explicit specs, not real-world issues described in vague natural language across large repositories.
AI.method: A pipeline that (1) writes a formal specification for the new code, (2) summarizes the existing functions the code calls as axioms, and (3) admits an instance only after both mechanical and adversarial gates agree. Applied to SWE-bench Verified to produce SWE-Proof (and extended to SWE-bench Pro). Evaluation across two frontier models comparing verification vs tests, and analyzing spec-writing performance.
AI.result: Verification catches 25–50% of counterexamples among test-passing patches; a correct formal specification raises Opus 4.8 resolution from 85% to 95%. 500 real issues formalized as SWE-Proof; self-written specs perform poorly in audit (62% pass). Faithfulness is the main failure mode, with 89% of unresolved vs 47% resolved instances failing, indicating faithful specification synthesis remains an open problem.
AI.conclusion: Formal verification can outperform tests in catching issues and increasing resolution, but the bottleneck is generating faithful, complete specifications; unaided models offer limited gains, and faithful spec synthesis remains a concrete open research challenge.

title: When to Waddle: A Comparative Study of Bipedal Torso-Stabilization on Low-Friction Surfaces
summary: Low-friction surfaces challenge bipedal locomotion by limiting the contact forces available during stepping. Inspired by penguin waddling, we investigate how lateral torso motion and center of mass (COM) placement affect locomotion as surface friction changes. Using a five-actuator biped, we compare an upright-gait strategy with a penguin-inspired torso-over-stance-leg strategy across multiple COM placements in simulation and hardware. In the 3-D simulator MuJoCo, we sweep through sinusoidal leg and hip actuation parameters across four friction coefficients mu = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7. In simulation, torso-over-stance-leg motion produces more successful controllers and higher forward speeds at low friction, with the highest speed occurring for the high-COM configuration. Hardware experiments show the same low-friction speed trend: at mu=0.12, torso-over-stance-leg motion increases forward speed and reduces cost of transport at both tested COM ratios, and the higher COM also improves both measures. The high-COM penguin configuration is the fastest and most energy efficient while maintaining low sideways foot motion. At mu=0.45, the COM trend reverses: the lower-COM configurations are faster and more energy efficient, while gait strategy has little effect on forward speed but still changes sideways foot motion. These results show that the effects of lateral torso motion and COM placement depend on the available friction, and that forward speed, energy use, and slip-related foot motion can be modulated with a penguin-inspired torso motion on hardware.

AI.tldr: Penguin-inspired torso-over-stance-leg strategy improves low-friction biped locomotion; COM placement and friction level determine optimal speed and energy efficiency, with a high-COM advantage at very low friction but lower-COM advantageous at moderate friction.
AI.motivation: Low-friction surfaces limit contact forces; inspired by penguin waddling, examine how lateral torso motion and COM placement affect locomotion across friction levels.
AI.method: Five-actuator biped; compare upright-gait vs penguin-inspired torso-over-stance-leg across multiple COM placements. MuJoCo simulations across mu=0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7; hardware experiments at mu≈0.12 and 0.45; measure forward speed, cost of transport, sideways foot motion.
AI.result: Simulation: torso-over-stance-leg yields more successful controllers and higher forward speeds at low friction; highest speed with high-COM. Hardware: at mu=0.12, torso-over-stance-leg increases speed and reduces COT for both COM ratios; higher-COM improves both. High-COM penguin config fastest and most energy-efficient with limited sideways motion. At mu=0.45, trend reverses: lower-COM faster and more energy-efficient; gait strategy largely affects sideways motion but not forward speed.
AI.conclusion: Effect of lateral torso motion and COM placement is friction-dependent; penguin-inspired torso motion can modulate speed and energy use and reduce slip; optimal configuration shifts with friction.

title: The Communication Bottleneck: A Round-Trip Study of Tree-Structured Expression Serialization in Language Models
summary: When language models reason in chain-of-thought or exchange free-text intermediates, they serialize structured information into natural language. How much tree-structured compositional content survives this bottleneck? We propose a round-trip protocol that answers this question empirically for tree-structured expressions. A generator converts a procedurally generated arithmetic expression into a word problem, a separate extractor recovers the expression from the word problem alone, and symbolic equivalence provides an exact oracle. Evaluating all pairwise combinations of sixteen models yields a communication matrix whose marginals separate generation quality from extraction quality. Three main findings emerge. First, the channel is lossy and asymmetric: swapping which model generates and which extracts shifts accuracy by up to 60.4 points, and the best pair reaches 92.9% by combining different models on each end rather than the same model on both. Second, at least 73.6% of round-trip failures originate at generation, and difficulty is driven by tree structure (operator count, depth, right-branching) rather than model family. Third, the channel is trainable: ~3600 fine-tuning examples that share the evaluation's operators and tree shapes lift every open-weight model above untrained Gemini-3.1-Pro, an upper bound under matched semantics. A disjoint-domain regime with new operators and vocabulary also raises every open-weight model, confirming the gain is not an artifact of matched semantics, though a gap to the frontier remains. Together these results identify tree-structured expression serialization as a primary limiting factor when models communicate hierarchical structure through natural language.

AI.tldr: Tree-structured expressions are significantly degraded when serialized to natural language during reasoning, as shown by a round-trip protocol across 16 models; generation quality drives most failures; cross-model end-points and fine-tuning improve performance, but a frontier gap remains.
AI.motivation: Assess how much tree-structured, hierarchical content survives natural-language intermediates in language-model reasoning, and whether the process can be improved via model specialization, training, or cross-endpoints.
AI.method: 1) Procedurally generate arithmetic expressions with explicit tree structure. 2) Use a generator to turn expressions into word problems. 3) Use an extractor to recover the expression from the word problem alone. 4) Use exact symbolic equivalence as the ground-truth oracle. 5) Evaluate all pairwise combinations of 16 models, constructing a communication matrix with marginals for generation vs extraction quality. 6) Analyze failures to determine whether they originate primarily at generation vs extraction and how tree properties affect difficulty. 7) Fine-tune ~3600 examples sharing operators/tree shapes to test trainability; compare with open-weight baselines (e.g., Gemini-3.1-Pro). 8) Extend with a disjoint-domain regime using new operators/vocabulary to test generality of gains.
AI.result: The communication channel is lossy and asymmetric: swapping generation vs extraction changes accuracy by up to 60.4 points; the best pair achieves 92.9% accuracy when using different models at the two ends. Generation is the main source of round-trip failures (≥73.6%), with difficulty driven by tree features (operator count, depth, right-branching) rather than model family. Fine-tuning with ~3600 examples lifts all open-weight models above the strongest baseline; disjoint-domain gains persist, indicating improvements are not solely due to matched semantics. Overall, tree-structured expression serialization is a primary bottleneck for conveying hierarchical structure via natural language.
AI.conclusion: Tree-structured expression serialization poses a fundamental bottleneck for communicating hierarchical structure through natural language in model reasoning. Improvements require cross-endpoint strategies (mixing models), targeted fine-tuning on structural shapes, and broader-domain generalization; current gains close part of the gap to frontier but do not reach it.

title: Think Locally, Refine Globally for Memory-Efficient 3D Reconstruction
summary: We propose LoG-VGGT, a memory-efficient framework for long-sequence 3D reconstruction that balances local temporal modeling with global camera consistency. Instead of relying on full global attention, our method introduces cross-window attention at a small subset of transformer blocks, enabling effective information propagation across adjacent temporal windows while keeping memory usage bounded. To mitigate long-term pose drift, we further design a global camera consistency refinement module, where camera tokens interact with compact register tokens via cross-attention to enforce scene-level constraints across the entire sequence. This design enables joint optimization of camera representations and significantly improves long-horizon pose stability without incurring the high cost of sequence-wide attention. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LoG-VGGT achieves improved depth accuracy and robust camera pose estimation across multiple long-sequence benchmarks, while delivering competitive streaming reconstruction performance.

AI.tldr: A memory-efficient long-sequence 3D reconstruction framework (LoG-VGGT) that combines limited cross-window attention with a global camera consistency refinement to balance local temporal modeling and global pose stability under bounded memory.
AI.motivation: Long-sequence 3D reconstruction faces memory bottlenecks and pose drift when using full sequence-wide attention. The goal is to achieve scalable, stable reconstruction by restricting attention to cross-window interactions while enforcing global consistency.
AI.method: 1) Employ cross-window attention in a small subset of transformer blocks to propagate information across adjacent temporal windows with bounded memory; 2) Introduce a global camera consistency refinement module where camera tokens interact with compact register tokens via cross-attention to enforce scene-level constraints across the entire sequence; 3) Jointly optimize camera representations with the scene model to improve long-horizon pose stability.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation shows improved depth accuracy and robust camera pose estimation on long-sequence benchmarks, with competitive streaming reconstruction performance.
AI.conclusion: LoG-VGGT delivers improved long-horizon pose stability and depth accuracy while maintaining bounded memory, offering a scalable approach for long-sequence 3D reconstruction without resorting to full sequence-wide attention.

title: Reliability-Centered Evaluation of Sparse Longitudinal CT Lesion-Size Forecasting with Conformal Interval Calibration and Gompertz-Inspired Regularization
summary: Sparse longitudinal CT follow-up limits lesion-size forecasting when only a few prior observations are available. We constructed a five-visit DLT-derived same-lesion trajectory benchmark from DeepLesion and Deep Lesion Tracker (DLT), yielding 205 trajectories from 129 patients. We compared an exploratory conventional sparse-to-final analysis with a primary fixed visit-index horizon design predicting the common log change from T3 to T4 while progressively adding earlier observations, evaluating predictive accuracy, uncertainty reliability, post-hoc conformal interval calibration, subgroup performance, and Gompertz-inspired trajectory regularization. The evaluated methods showed partially overlapping point-prediction accuracy but distinct uncertainty behavior. Mean held-out RMSE across ten training seeds was 0.4726, 0.4305, 0.4499, and 0.4513 for m = 1, 2, 3, 4, indicating the lowest mean RMSE at m = 2; additional history did not improve RMSE. At m = 4, raw Cohort-Level Feature GP coverage was near the 95% nominal level, whereas MC Dropout, Deep Ensemble, and residual-scale intervals were conservative. Patient-level conformal calibration generally produced near-nominal or conservative coverage at the cost of wider intervals. Patient-grouped development cross-validation selected lambda* = 0 for the Gompertz-inspired term. A global population reference frequently opposed lesion-level change directions, and prediction difficulty varied across anatomical subgroups. Overall, additional historical observations provided limited predictive benefit once the prediction horizon was controlled, while predictive accuracy, uncertainty reliability, and trajectory consistency did not necessarily improve together, and should be evaluated jointly in sparse longitudinal imaging.

AI.tldr: Sparse longitudinal CT lesion forecasting with a fixed horizon shows limited benefit from extra historical observations; best RMSE occurs with two prior visits. Uncertainty calibration varies by method (GP, MC dropout, deep ensembles, residual-scale); conformal calibration is near nominal to conservative, often yielding wider intervals. Gompertz-inspired regularization selected with lambda*=0. Global population trends may conflict with lesion-level directions, with performance varying by anatomical subgroup. Overall, accuracy, uncertainty, and trajectory consistency do not consistently improve together in sparse, horizon-limited settings.
AI.motivation: Address predictive forecasting of lesion size in sparse longitudinal CT data when only a few prior observations exist, using a realistic five-visit trajectory benchmark and multiple uncertainty-aware methods.
AI.method: Create a five-visit trajectory benchmark from DeepLesion and DLT, compare sparse-to-final analysis with a fixed horizon predicting log-change from T3 to T4, progressively add earlier visits, and evaluate (i) predictive accuracy (RMSE), (ii) uncertainty reliability, (iii) post-hoc conformal interval calibration, (iv) subgroup performance, and (v) Gompertz-inspired trajectory regularization. Assess multiple uncertainty methods (GP-based, MC dropout, deep ensembles, residual-scale intervals) and a Gompertz term with lambda*. Train across ten seeds.
AI.result: Mean hold-out RMSE across m = 1..4 were 0.4726, 0.4305, 0.4499, 0.4513, with the minimum at m=2. At m=4, raw cohort-level GP coverage approached 95% nominal, while MC Dropout, Deep Ensemble, and residual-scale intervals were conservative. Patient-level conformal calibration yielded near-nominal or conservative coverage but wider intervals. Lambda* for the Gompertz term was 0, and predictions varied in performance across anatomical subgroups; history added beyond horizon did not improve RMSE. Overall, accuracy, uncertainty reliability, and trajectory consistency did not monotonically improve together; joint assessment is recommended for sparse longitudinal imaging.
AI.conclusion: Additional historical data offer limited predictive benefit when the horizon is fixed; accuracy, uncertainty, and trajectory consistency may diverge, highlighting the need for joint evaluation of these aspects in sparse longitudinal imaging scenarios.

title: Robust Structureless Monocular Visual Inertial Initialization Exploiting Line Features and Vanishing Points
summary: Accurate initialization is essential for reliable visual-inertial odometry (VIO), but it is often ill-conditioned under degenerate motions. Existing methods typically require restrictive excitation motions to ensure sufficient observability or rely on computationally expensive 3D structure reconstruction, limiting efficient and practical deployment. To address these limitations, we propose SLIM-init, a structureless monocular VIO initializer that directly exploits geometric constraints from tracked 2D line features without explicit 3D landmark reconstruction. Specifically, SLIM-init leverages line-derived vanishing points (VPs) as translation-invariant orientation cues to provide robust rotation-only constraints under degenerate scenarios such as low-parallax or translation-dominant motions. It further incorporates a line epipolar residual to constrain translation and a line-normal projection residual to improve the conditioning of linear alignment, enhancing the accuracy and robustness of initial state estimation. Extensive experiments on a public benchmark and challenging custom degenerate-motion sequences demonstrate improved accuracy and robustness over state-of-the-art initialization methods. The source code is available at: https://github.com/cjunwan/SLIM-init.

AI.tldr: A structureless monocular VIO initializer (SLIM-init) uses 2D line features to infer rotation via vanishing points and jointly constrains translation via line epipolar and line-normal residuals, avoiding 3D reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Existing VIO initializers require restrictive motions or expensive 3D reconstruction; a robust, efficient initialization under degenerate motion is needed.
AI.method: Leverage vanishing points from tracked lines as translation-invariant orientation cues to constrain rotation; apply a line epipolar residual to constrain translation; use a line-normal projection residual to improve linear conditioning; all without reconstructing 3D landmarks.
AI.result: Experiments on public benchmarks and custom degenerate-motion sequences show improved accuracy and robustness compared with state-of-the-art initialization methods.
AI.conclusion: SLIM-init offers robust, efficient initialization under degenerate motions by exploiting 2D line geometry, avoiding 3D landmark reconstruction; code available at GitHub.

title: Learning-to-Optimize as the Missing Architectural Layer of AI-Native Networks
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is becoming a fundamental design principle of future AI-native communication networks, enabling autonomous resource management, adaptive control, and zero-touch network operation. While current AI-native architectures increasingly embed intelligence across network functions, they provide little guidance on how optimisation knowledge should be systematically generated, transferred, and exploited by AI models. This paper argues that the Learning-to-Optimize (L2O) represents the missing architectural layer between optimisation and AI-native intelligence. Rather than viewing optimisation merely as an online decision engine, the proposed paradigm redefines optimisation algorithms as offline knowledge generators that produce high-quality supervisory information for neural surrogate models. The resulting models inherit optimisation expertise while enabling low-latency runtime inference suitable for dynamic network environments. A generic four-stage L2O workflow is introduced, comprising optimisation, knowledge generation, surrogate learning, and runtime inference. Unlike existing Learning-to-Optimize approaches, which primarily focus on algorithm acceleration, the proposed framework establishes L2O as an architectural abstraction applicable across heterogeneous communication and computing systems. The proposed paradigm is illustrated by an NR-V2X relay-selection problem, in which optimisation-generated solutions from a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) solver are used to train a Graph Neural Network that can reproduce near-optimal decisions in real time. The presented perspective positions Learning-to-Optimize as a key architectural enabler for future AI-native networks.

AI.tldr: L2O positions optimization as an offline knowledge generator that feeds neural surrogates, creating a four-stage workflow (optimization, knowledge generation, surrogate learning, runtime inference) to enable low-latency AI-native networks; demonstrated via MILP-derived data training a GNN for NR-V2X relay selection.
AI.motivation: Current AI-native networks embed intelligence but lack systematic methods to generate and transfer optimization knowledge to AI models; there is a need for an architectural layer that leverages optimization expertise for real-time, heterogeneous networks.
AI.method: Propose a generic four-stage Learning-to-Optimize workflow: (1) optimization using traditional solvers; (2) knowledge generation by producing supervisory data from optimal solutions; (3) surrogate learning by training neural models (e.g., Graph Neural Networks) on the generated data; (4) runtime inference by deploying lightweight surrogates for real-time decisions. Illustrate with NR-V2X relay-selection where MILP solutions train a GNN to mimic near-optimal decisions.
AI.result: The surrogate model reproduces near-optimal decisions in real time, enabling low-latency operation in dynamic networks; the framework is proposed as broadly applicable across heterogeneous systems, beyond mere acceleration.
AI.conclusion: Learning-to-Optimize is presented as a foundational architectural abstraction for future AI-native networks, enabling systematic knowledge generation from optimization to empower AI models.

title: ME-Dex 1.0: Bringing Heterogeneous Tactile Sensing into World Action Modeling
summary: World Action Models bring the predictive capabilities of video models into robot action generation, providing a rich foundation for modeling future visual states. Tactile sensing complements this foundation with direct measurements of physical interaction. Some existing methods use tactile features as conditioning inputs without jointly predicting future tactile states, visual observations, and actions. Our key insight is that tactile signals, like video, provide observations of the evolving world state and should be modeled as future observations alongside video. We present ME-Dex-1.0 (MachEmbodied-Dex-1.0), a unified World Action Tactile Model for joint visual, tactile, and action learning. ME-Dex-1.0 adopts a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture comprising a Video Expert, a Tactile Expert, and an Action Expert, all trained with flow matching. We use shared attention connects the experts in intermediate layers, allowing action generation to draw on learned representations of visual and tactile dynamics during joint denoising. To support multi-source heterogeneous tactile inputs, a Canonical Hand Model and a Unified Tactile Autoencoder map tactile observations from different embodiments and sensing layouts into shared spatial and latent spaces. To address the limited availability of paired visual, tactile, and action data, we develop the Agentic Tactile Data Engine, an agent-based data production platform. It supplements RoboTwin and DexJoCo with tactile data recorded directly from force sensors during trajectory replay in simulation. Experiments on the RoboTwin, DexJoCo, and ManiFeel simulation platforms, together with real robot evaluations, demonstrate improved manipulation performance using both grippers and dexterous hands equipped with tactile sensing.

AI.tldr: ME-Dex-1.0 introduces a unified World Action Tactile Model that jointly predicts visual, tactile, and action trajectories using a Mixture-of-Transformers, with cross-modal sharing, cross-embodiment tactile alignment, and synthetic tactile data generation to improve manipulation in simulation and on real robots.
AI.motivation: Extend predictive world models to tactile sensing, treating tactile signals as future observations alongside video to enable coherent multi-modal planning and improved manipulation robustness.
AI.method: Mixture-of-Transformers with three experts (Video, Tactile, Action); shared intermediate-attention between experts; flow matching objective for multi-modal prediction; Canonical Hand Model and Unified Tactile Autoencoder to map diverse tactile inputs into a common space; Agentic Tactile Data Engine to generate tactile data from forced-sensor trajectories in simulation (RoboTwin, DexJoCo, ManiFeel); evaluation on multiple simulators and real robots (grippers and dexterous hands).
AI.result: Joint video-tactile-action generation improves manipulation performance across different hardware and platforms, demonstrated in simulation (RoboTwin, DexJoCo, ManiFeel) and real robots.
AI.conclusion: A unified, multi-modal predictive framework can leverage tactile dynamics alongside visual dynamics to enhance manipulation; cross-embodiment tactile alignment and synthetic data generation enable broader applicability and potential gains in sample efficiency and generalization.

title: MIRCID: Inferred Hub-miRNAs Drive Cross-Task Improvements in Drug Mechanistic Modeling
summary: Drug mechanism-of-action (MoA) modeling commonly relies on perturbational transcriptomes, but matched microRNA (miRNA) measurements are often unavailable. Inferred regulatory features offer a scalable way to reuse these data. Here, we present MIRCID, a framework comparing gene expression with inferred transcription factor (TF) activity and miRNA expression across pathway classification and similarity-based MoA retrieval. HubmiRNet infers 414 pan-cancer hub miRNAs (HubmiRs) from 977 L1000 landmark genes, achieving a Pearson correlation coefficient of 87.72\%; its 1,298-output variant also outperformed SiCmiR on the full-miRNA task (71.21\% versus 67.30\%). In the evaluated comparisons, miRNA augmentation provided more consistent gains than TF activity. Generic embedding controls showed model-dependent utility, while complementarity analyses identified a distinct, partially linearly recoverable representation that retained gene-derived structure. Illustrative rescue cases linked improved classification to biologically plausible miRNA patterns in samples with weak transcriptional signatures. These findings support inferred HubmiRs as a biologically informed recoding of transcriptomic data for perturbational drug modeling, while leaving recovery of measured perturbational miRNA responses to further validation.

AI.tldr: Framework MIRCID uses inferred miRNA and TF activity to augment MoA modeling; HubmiRNet's hub miRNAs enable strong performance gains and biologically plausible patterns, suggesting inferred miRNAs can recode transcriptomic data for drug mechanism studies, with validation needed for measured miRNA recovery.
AI.motivation: Perturbational transcriptomes often lack matched miRNA measurements; inferring regulatory features offers scalable reuse of data for drug mechanism modeling.
AI.method: Introduces MIRCID framework comparing gene expression against inferred TF activity and miRNA expression for pathway classification and MoA retrieval. HubmiRNet infers 414 HubmiRs from 977 L1000 genes; a 1,298-output variant outperforms SiCmiR on full-miRNA task.
AI.result: HubmiRNet achieves Pearson correlation 87.72%. The 1,298-output variant achieves 71.21% vs. 67.30% for SiCmiR on the full-miRNA task. In evaluations, miRNA augmentation yields more consistent gains than TF activity; generic embedding controls show model-dependent utility; complementarity analyses reveal a distinct, partially linearly recoverable representation preserving gene-derived structure; rescue cases link improved classification to biologically plausible miRNA patterns in samples with weak transcriptional signatures.
AI.conclusion: Inferred HubmiRs provide a biologically informed recoding of transcriptomic data for perturbational drug modeling and can enhance MoA analysis, though recovering measured perturbational miRNA responses requires further validation.

title: Stochastic Neural Signed Swept Volume for Real-time Chance-Constrained Trajectory Optimization
summary: Collision-free motion planning requires reliable collision models from sensed environments and validation of states along a continuous trajectory. To make this tractable, most planners check for collision at discrete states along continuous trajectories against a single determinized model of the environment, introducing a trade-off between safety and computational efficiency. While continuous collision checking approaches that approximate the swept volume of the robot exist, they are computationally expensive or overly conservative. Data-driven approaches can learn the swept volume; however, these neural models are susceptible to approximation errors and are therefore often limited to serving as coarse filters for downstream collision checkers. In this work, we propose to learn a signed distance function of the swept volume as a probabilistic field, enabling quantification of epistemic uncertainty, incorporation of perception noise, and eventual integration into a chance-constrained trajectory optimization framework. We demonstrate our approach on challenging high-dimensional manipulation problems with significant sensor noise, both in simulation and on real hardware.

AI.tldr: Probabilistic SDF of the robot's swept volume for continuous collision checking enables uncertainty-aware planning.
AI.motivation: Collision checking along continuous trajectories is computationally expensive and often conservative when using discrete checks on a single environment model; perception noise and model error motivate probabilistic, data-driven swept-volume representations.
AI.method: Learn a signed distance function (SDF) of the swept volume as a probabilistic field to quantify epistemic uncertainty and incorporate perception noise, then integrate this into a chance-constrained trajectory optimization framework.
AI.result: Validated on challenging high-dimensional manipulation tasks with significant sensor noise, in both simulation and real hardware.
AI.conclusion: Introduces a probabilistic, uncertainty-aware approach to continuous collision checking that bridges data-driven swept-volume modeling with chance-constrained planning, improving safety-efficiency trade-offs in noisy, high-dimensional manipulation.

title: Dual-Interest Sequential Product Recommendation With Multi-Granular SSM
summary: Sequential recommendation aims to predict the next item a user will interact with based on their historical behavior. Advances in Transformers have significantly improved sequential recommendation but are still limited by cost efficiency. Although State Space Models (SSMs) have recently enabled efficient long-range modeling, most existing methods encode each item with a single static contextual role, overlooking the phenomenon of item polysemy. In fact, the same item often plays different semantic roles depending on user context, and existing methods are limited in capturing dynamic behavior across different temporal granularities. In this work, we propose DSRec, a novel dual-interest cross-SSM model that explicitly disentangles item roles across long-term and short-term semantic context. Sequential items are encoded into long-term interest embeddings that capture stable preferences via historical aggregation, and a short-term interest branch that emphasizes local session intent modulated by inter-click time intervals. These interest embeddings are processed through distinct SSM encoders: a full-sequence Mamba for long-term modeling, and a time-modulated SSM that dynamically adjusts state evolution based on temporal gaps. To enable effective cross-granularity alignment, we adopt a residual cross-fusion mechanism that exchanges contextual information between the two branches while preserving semantic independence. Experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate that DSRec outperforms other state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: DSRec introduces a dual-branch, cross-SSM sequential recommender that disentangles long-term and short-term item roles, using a full-sequence Mamba for long-range encoding and a time-modulated SSM for short-term, with residual cross-fusion for cross-granularity alignment, achieving state-of-the-art results on public benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Addresses item polysemy and multi-granularity temporal dynamics overlooked by prior static-embedding SSM approaches; seeks efficient long-range modeling via SSM and dynamic adaptation to temporal gaps.
AI.method: Two-branch architecture: long-term branch encodes stable preferences via historical aggregation; short-term branch models local session intent using inter-click time intervals. Encoders: full-sequence Mamba for long-term modeling; time-modulated SSM for short-term state evolution based on temporal gaps. Cross-granularity alignment via residual cross-fusion preserving semantic independence.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on public benchmarks shows DSRec outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
AI.conclusion: Disentangling long- and short-term item semantics with cross-granularity SSMs and cross-fusion improves recommendation quality; confirms the importance of temporal dynamics and polysemy in sequential recommendation.

title: CompAdapt: Adaptable Composite Motion Modeling for Physics-Consistent Text-to-Video Generation
comment: 23 pages, 4 figures. Submitted to the 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026). Project page: https://makapic.github.io/CompAdapt/
summary: While diffusion-based text-to-video (T2V) models have demonstrated impressive capability in generating realistic and temporally coherent videos, they often fail to respect fundamental physical dynamics. Although recent physics-constrained methods incorporate explicit dynamics priors to improve physical plausibility, they remain limited to simple single-type motions, depend on manually specified parameters, and struggle to generalize to unseen physical laws. In this work, we propose CompAdapt, a physics-consistent T2V framework for adaptable generation across complex real-world scenarios. It extends neural dynamics modeling beyond single-type motions to encompass composite physical behaviors, including coupled motions, multi-stage transitions, and multi-object collisions. Furthermore, CompAdapt translates natural language prompts into structured physical semantics, enabling end-to-end specification of motion types, temporal relations, and initial physical parameters. To generalize to novel physical environments, CompAdapt introduces dynamics-aware prior matching, achieving one-shot adaptation without retraining the core dynamics module. In addition, a physics-aware latent feature fusion module improves visual fidelity under fast and complex motion. Experiments on physics-focused T2V benchmarks demonstrate that CompAdapt improves physical consistency over both general T2V models and physics-constrained baselines, while preserving high visual quality and adaptability to unseen dynamics. The project page is available at https://makapic.github.io/CompAdapt/ .

AI.tldr: CompAdapt is a physics-consistent text-to-video framework enabling adaptable generation across complex real-world dynamics by learning composite physical behaviors, translating prompts into structured physical semantics, and enabling one-shot adaptation via dynamics-aware prior matching, with a physics-aware latent fusion module to improve motion fidelity.
AI.motivation: Address the mismatch between diffusion-based T2V and real-world physics, which currently handles only simple motions and requires manual priors/retraining; enable generalization to unseen dynamics and composite behaviors while maintaining visual quality.
AI.method: Extends neural dynamics beyond single-type motions to coupled motions, multi-stage transitions, and multi-object collisions; translates natural language prompts into structured physics semantics; dynamics-aware prior matching for one-shot adaptation; physics-aware latent feature fusion for fast, complex motion.
AI.result: Empirical results on physics-focused T2V benchmarks show improved physical consistency over general T2V models and physics-constrained baselines, with preserved visual quality and adaptability to unseen dynamics; project page available.
AI.conclusion: CompAdapt demonstrates that combining structured physical semantics, adaptive priors, and physics-aware fusion yields robust, adaptable, and physically plausible video generation in real-world scenarios, paving the way for more realistic physics-aware T2V systems.

title: Multi-Subject Pretraining Enables Short-Calibration Personalization for Closed-Corpus Surface EMG Speech Decoding
summary: Surface electromyography (sEMG)-based silent speech interfaces are limited by cross-user variability and calibration burden. We study a limited-data setting in which each of 27 speech-typical participants contributed less than 0.5 h of data (21.3 min on average) across Aloud and Mimed speech. Within a closed 50-sentence corpus, we used leave-one-subject-out evaluation, initializing from a released single-subject checkpoint, pretraining on non-held-out participants, and fine-tuning on the target participant. This pipeline achieved 21.7% character error rate (CER) and 31.9% word error rate (WER), compared with 49.3% CER without target-subject calibration and 68.0% CER for direct checkpoint fine-tuning. Multi-subject pretraining from random initialization followed by fine-tuning reached 44.9% CER and did not converge under the fixed schedule in 5 of 27 folds, indicating substantial optimization and accuracy benefits from checkpoint initialization. Macro-averaged CER declined from 74.4% with one pretraining participant to 21.7% with 26. Three minutes of target-subject calibration achieved 20.5% CER and 31.7% WER, with no statistically significant difference from the full approximately 13-min pool (21.7% CER and 31.9% WER). A subject-specific adapter provided no detectable benefit. Excluding the five evaluation sentences from all sEMG model-training data increased CER and WER to 78.6% and 99.9%. These results support short-calibration personalization in a standardized-montage, closed-corpus setting.

AI.tldr: Few-shot personalization with checkpoint-initialized pretraining substantially closes cross-user sEMG silent speech gaps; short calibration (~3 minutes) rivals full calibration (~13 minutes).
AI.motivation: Address cross-subject variability and calibration burden in sEMG-based silent speech interfaces under limited data.
AI.method: Leave-one-subject-out evaluation on 27 participants with <0.5 h each; compare initialization strategies (single-subject checkpoint, multi-subject pretraining, random init); fine-tuning on target; test with/without target calibration; evaluate macro CER and WER; test a subject-specific adapter and hold-out sentences.
AI.result: Target-subject calibration (3 min) yields 20.5% CER and 31.7% WER, statistically similar to full calibration (21.7% CER, 31.9% WER). Using a released single-subject checkpoint for initialization improves performance; random initialization with multi-subject pretraining often fails to converge. One pretraining subject reduces macro CER from 74.4% to 21.7% across folds. A subject-specific adapter provides no detectable benefit. Excluding evaluation sentences vastly degrades performance (CER 78.6%, WER 99.9%).
AI.conclusion: Short calibration with checkpoint-based pretraining effectively mitigates cross-subject variability in a standardized-montage, closed-corpus setting; initialization choice and calibration strategy critically determine performance.

title: Visual Navigation Transformer with Pose Attention
summary: Learned navigation policies typically consume observations as a temporally ordered history, with positional encodings tying each observation to when it was seen, making it difficult to reuse experience from earlier traversals of an environment. Systems that do reuse such experience usually construct an explicit representation, such as a map or a topological graph, and plan on it. We propose VNT-PA (Visual Navigation Transformer with Pose Attention), a transformer planner whose context is a set of depth keyframes indexed by camera pose. With camera poses as positional encoding, attention depends on the pose differences between keyframes rather than on their temporal order. VNT-PA is trained to imitate a shortest-path planner operating on the ground-truth scene mesh, predicting actions by querying the spatial context with only its current pose and the goal position. On point-goal navigation in HM3D validation scenes, VNT-PA reaches 93.3% success and 90.4% success weighted by path length (SPL), outperforming baselines that encode the same context as a temporal sequence or treat pose as an input feature, in both navigation performance and training efficiency. Because the spatial context is a pose-indexed set, frames from different trajectories can be fused at test time. The planner also degrades more gracefully under localization noise than a conventional baseline which plans on explicit maps. These results show that pose-stamped experience can serve directly as the environment representation for a learned planner, and that making attention depend on pose differences, rather than on temporal order, speeds up training and improves long-horizon navigation.

AI.tldr: VNT-PA introduces a transformer-based planner that uses a pose-indexed set of depth keyframes and pose-difference attention to imitate a shortest-path planner, enabling efficient long-horizon navigation and test-time fusion of trajectories, outperforming temporal-sequence baselines and showing robustness to localization noise.
AI.motivation: Reuse of experience across traversals is hindered by temporally ordered observations; explicit maps help but have limitations; propose a pose-indexed spatial context that can be fused across trajectories and trained efficiently.
AI.method: A transformer planner (VNT-PA) that takes as context a set of depth keyframes indexed by camera pose; uses camera poses as positional encodings; attention is driven by pose differences rather than temporal order; trained via imitation learning to imitate a shortest-path planner on the ground-truth scene mesh; inputs: current pose and goal position; outputs: action predictions.
AI.result: On HM3D validation for point-goal navigation, achieves 93.3% success and 90.4% SPL; outperforms baselines that encode the same context as a temporal sequence or treat pose as a feature; training is more efficient; frames from different trajectories can be fused at test time; shows greater robustness to localization noise than explicit-map baselines.
AI.conclusion: Pose-stamped experience can serve as the environment representation for a learned planner; pose-difference-based attention accelerates training and improves long-horizon navigation; enables cross-trajectory fusion through a pose-indexed context.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Centroid-Guided Contrastive Loss for Structured Fraudulent Job Posting Detection
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, 8 tables. Submitted to IEEE Open Journal of the Computer Society. Code: https://github.com/ali-ahmed925/CGCL_code
summary: Fraudulent job posting detection aims to identify job advertisements that are corrupted either through fake content, misleading information, or negative intent, disrupting the online eco-system of job-seekers and employers. Existing studies in this domain lack effective methods to simultaneously achieve high accuracy and meaningful structure of latent-space representations that capture subtleties among fake posts. To this end, we propose Centroid-Guided Contrastive Loss (CGCL), a loss function which unifies classification with densely formulated clustering to consistently reshape latent-space through a centroid-driven top-$k$ push-and-pull mechanism. The complementary nature of CGCL enables the model to enforce accurate decision boundaries and maintain high clustering compactness, effectively capturing both class separability and latent structure. Extensive experiments demonstrate the state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance of our method on EMSCAD, a public benchmark dataset. The code associated with this work is available at: https://github.com/ali-ahmed925/CGCL_code

AI.tldr: Proposes Centroid-Guided Contrastive Loss (CGCL) for fraudulent job posting detection, combining classification with dense clustering via a centroid-driven top-k push-and-pull to shape latent representations; achieves SOTA on EMSCAD; code released.
AI.motivation: Addresses the gap between high accuracy and meaningful latent structures in fake/post detection by jointly optimizing classification and clustering.
AI.method: Introduces CGCL loss that unifies discriminative learning and clustering; leverages centroid guidance and top-k push-pull to reshape latent space.
AI.result: Empirical results claim state-of-the-art performance on EMSCAD benchmark; code available.
AI.conclusion: CGCL enforces accurate decision boundaries while maintaining latent-space compactness, effectively capturing class separability and latent structure in fraudulent posting detection.

title: PSEE: Progressive Sensor Event Expansion for Point-Supervised Temporal Action Localization
summary: Temporal action localization (TAL) in wearable sensor streams identifies action classes and temporal boundaries, enabling finer-grained activity understanding than conventional action recognition. However, training typically requires costly start--end annotations for every action instance. To reduce this burden, we study point-supervised TAL, where each instance is labeled with only one timestamp and its class. We propose Progressive Sensor Event Expansion (PSEE), which combines semantic activations, sensor-specific transition evidence, and adaptive temporal ownership to recover point-supervised pseudo segments. These segments supervise standard TAL detectors without modifying their inference procedures. Cross-subject experiments on four inertial-sensing benchmarks demonstrate improved pseudo-boundary quality over adapted point-supervised baselines, compatibility with different TAL detectors, and robustness to point sampling. Code is available at https://github.com/joeeeeyin/PSEE.

AI.tldr: Proposes Progressive Sensor Event Expansion (PSEE) to convert point-supervised TAL into trained detectors by recovering pseudo segments from semantic activations, transition evidence, and adaptive ownership; improves boundary quality and is compatible with various TAL detectors; code released.
AI.motivation: Reduce annotation burden in temporal action localization for wearable sensor streams by using only point labels, and recover useful segment supervision to train detectors.
AI.method: PSEE fuses semantic activations, sensor-specific transition cues, and adaptive temporal ownership to generate pseudo segments from single-point labels; these pseudo segments supervise standard TAL detectors without altering their inference.
AI.result: Cross-subject evaluation on four inertial-sensing benchmarks shows improved pseudo-boundary quality versus adapted point-supervised baselines, detector-agnostic compatibility, and robustness to point sampling.
AI.conclusion: PSEE provides an effective, detector-friendly mechanism to leverage point-supervised labels for TAL in wearable sensors, enabling practical reduction of annotation burden with maintained performance; code is available.

title: FairLMs: A Turnkey Library for Fairness in Language Models
summary: Fairness research on language models involves measuring bias, applying mitigation methods, and examining the evidence on which an evaluation rests. Existing tools offer complementary functionality through different interfaces, so combining them requires reconciling model interfaces, evidence formats, access constraints, and result types before applicability can be checked or methods compared. We introduce \textbf{FairLMs}, a Python library that connects these activities through explicit declarations of model capabilities and input requirements. It provides 33 intrinsic and extrinsic metrics, 14 mitigation components spanning four intervention categories, 14 dataset and scoring-instrument diagnostics, adapters for the three Transformer architectures and supported hosted completion APIs, and benchmark loaders. Declarations are checked before execution and results carry the configuration under which they were obtained, so that compatible components can be combined, methods compared under a common protocol, and workflows extended to new models and datasets. The source code is available at: https://github.com/FairLMs/FairLMs.
